South Korea’s Electrical Equipment Sector Recovered from 2017 Cyber Attack

SEOUL, June 8 — South Korea’s electrical equipment sector has since recovered from a major cyber attack in 2017 that temporarily disrupted production and deliveries at several firms, industry officials and analysts said this week.

The attack, which occurred in late October 2017, targeted the IT systems of four leading electrical equipment manufacturers, including Daehan Switchgear Co. and Koryo Power Systems Ltd. According to the Korea Association of Electrical Equipment Manufacturers, the attack involved ransomware that encrypted critical production and logistics data, forcing the affected firms to halt operations for up to a week.

“At the time, the attack paralyzed our order tracking and supply chain management systems,” said Kim Min-jun, a spokesperson for Daehan Switchgear Co. “We were unable to ship transformers and circuit breakers to our domestic and overseas customers for several days.”

Industry analysts estimate that the attack cost the sector at least 18 billion won ($16 million) in lost output and recovery expenses. “The 2017 incident was a wake-up call for the industry,” said Lee Soo-jin, an analyst at Seoul-based market research firm TechInsights Korea. “It exposed vulnerabilities in older IT infrastructure and highlighted the need for stronger cybersecurity protocols.”

The Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy at the time coordinated with affected companies and the National Police Agency’s cyber bureau to investigate the incident and restore operations. No perpetrators were publicly identified.

“Since then, we have invested heavily in cybersecurity and employee training,” said Park Ji-hoon, president of the Korea Association of Electrical Equipment Manufacturers. “While the attack caused significant disruption in 2017, no similar incidents have occurred since.”

Production and deliveries across the sector returned to normal by mid-November 2017, according to industry data. The incident has prompted ongoing efforts to enhance cyber resilience across South Korea’s electrical equipment firms.
